text:
alex: Heads-up — rolled out the runtime flag change for `prefix_cache.enabled` to canary (10% of prod) ~2m ago. Seeing request rate for dedicated-pool routes spike ~3x. Not sure why traffic pattern changed. anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: canary deploy `canary-2026-03-18-01` finished, 10% traffic routed to runtime-v2.

anya: I see the same in traces — batching window collapsed. telemetry shows batch_size median = 1 for the canary shard. :confused:

kevin: That would explain the token cost jump. Did the flag also alter `batching.policy`? The PR only mentioned `prefix_cache`.

alex: PR was small, only toggled cache and a tiny routing hint. here's the snippet I pushed:

```json
{
  "runtime_flags": {
    "prefix_cache.enabled": true,
    "prefix_cache.eviction_ms": 60000
  },
  "canary": {
    "percent": 10,
    "selector": "cookie:rw_experiment_v2"
  }
}
```

lisa: CI didn't set `service.batch_hint_ms` so runtime may have chosen adaptive=lowest. I can query logs for the canary shard.

sam: Dashboard quick note — quota consumption for dedicated-pool + user-facing routes jumped from ~120 QPS to ~360 QPS in the canary window. Not traffic — likely per-request amplification.

anya: I'm compiling trace snippets. Looks like `prepare_batch()` returns earlier when prefix cache hits are false, causing immediate flush. Cache miss rate for new keys is high on canary due to cookie selector skew.

kevin: Two immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the flag for canary, 2) force batching policy to `min(8, adaptive)` for canary. Which is faster?

alex: Rollback is fastest. Can someone run the rollback command?

lisa: On it. Running: `redwood deploy rollback --env=prod --canary=canary-2026-03-18-01`

deploy-bot: rollback started for canary-2026-03-18-01 by lisa.

sam: While that's happening, let's add a constraint to rollout UX: show estimated token/unit delta when toggling runtime flags that touch batching/caching. This would have flagged the change.

kevin: Agreed. Also propose a preflight check for any runtime flag that matches `/batch|cache|queue|latency/` to simulate cost delta on recent traffic sample.

anya: I can sketch a telemetry preflight: run a sampling job over 24h of routing traces and estimate batch sizes + token counts with and without the flag. Should be quick in infra.

alex: Nice. For immediate follow-up: 1) postmortem-ish note in #incidents with short timeline, 2) add the preflight task to eng-platform backlog, 3) UX work to show delta on rollout modal.

lisa: Rollback finished, traffic back to previous hosts. Quota and QPS stabilized.

sam: Confirming metrics normalized. Thanks.

kevin: Next steps — I will open a RFC for the preflight sim and a small runtime change to make batching policy deterministic during canaries unless explicitly overridden.

anya: I'll attach the traces and a small script to estimate batch impact.

alex: Great. Can we add an opt-in checkbox in console: "simulate cost & latency impact before rolling out" and default it on for flags that affect runtime?

kevin: Yes, UX + API change. I'll coordinate with product.

sam: Filing follow-ups: https://go/internal/tickets/ENG-PLAT-2234 (preflight), ENG-PLAT-2235 (console delta).

alex: Thanks everyone. Quick retro: can we also add a simple lint in PRs that touch runtime flags to remind to think about batching? small docs pointer should help. :thumbsup:
